interactionPlan.concept: The 2D Fourier Transform exhibits a reciprocal relationship between spatial size and frequency spread, as well as orientation preservation under rotation.
learningObjectives: After engaging with this figure, the student will understand how spatial scaling inversely affects frequency support (narrowing in space broadens in frequency).
The student will be able to explain why a horizontal spatial structure corresponds to a vertical spectral distribution.
The student will be able to demonstrate that rotating an image rotates its Fourier transform by the same angle.
interactionPlan.keyInsight: Squeezing a shape in space stretches its frequencies, and rotating it rotates its frequency fingerprint by the exact same angle.

interactions.label: Box Width
interactions.effect: Modifies the horizontal width of the white spatial box; as width increases, the horizontal spread of the DFT amplitude narrows into a tighter vertical line.
interactions.teaches: The inverse scaling relationship of the Fourier transform: wider spatial features correspond to lower, more concentrated frequency components.

interactions.label: Box Height
interactions.effect: Modifies the vertical height of the white spatial box; as height increases, the vertical spread of the DFT amplitude narrows into a tighter horizontal line.
interactions.teaches: The spatial-frequency reciprocity along the vertical axis, demonstrating spatial-frequency separability.

interactions.label: Rotation Angle
interactions.effect: Rotates the spatial box; both the DFT amplitude and phase patterns rotate in unison with the spatial shape.
interactions.teaches: The rotation property of the 2D Fourier transform, showing that frequency components rotate directly with their spatial source.

interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Three-panel layout displaying: 1. Spatial Image (64x64, black background with a centered, white, rotatable and resizable rectangle), 2. DFT Amplitude (centered 2D magnitude spectrum showing a 2D sinc-like cross pattern, log-scaled for visibility), and 3. DFT Phase (showing the alternating phase bands). All elements update dynamically as sliders are moved.
